target.title: fix(heartbeat): require explicit message targets on heartbeat runs
target.body:
Closes #103519

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with heartbeat agents would receive leaked `HEARTBEAT_OK` text in their DM (routed agent) or hit `@heartbeat` / `chat not found` errors (isolated agent) when a heartbeat turn called the general `message` tool without an explicit recipient.

## Why This Change Was Made

Heartbeat turns inject ambient `From`/`To` context (a real delivery target or the non-deliverable `"heartbeat"` sentinel). Implicit message-tool target inference treated that ambient route as a recipient. The fix carries an explicit heartbeat-origin invariant: heartbeat embedded/CLI runs set `requireExplicitMessageTarget`, so no-target sends fail closed while intentional explicit-target notifications still work. Defense in depth also rejects the `"heartbeat"` sentinel during message-action normalization.

## User Impact

- Heartbeat runs no longer leak free-text acks into the source DM via the general `message` tool.
- Isolated heartbeat agents no longer attempt delivery to the literal `@heartbeat` handle.
- Explicit-target heartbeat notifications still work.
- Prefer `heartbeat_respond` for structured heartbeat acks (unchanged).

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass).

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
    src/infra/outbound/message-action-normalization.test.ts \
    src/agents/tools/message-tool.test.ts \
    src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.test.ts
# 21 + 120 + 239 tests passed

$ OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 pnpm exec node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- \
    src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.ts \
    src/infra/outbound/message-action-normalization.ts \
    src/infra/outbound/targets.ts \
    src/agents/tools/message-tool.ts
# typecheck core + core tests OK; lint 0 errors; import-cycle 0
```

Focused behavior cases:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/message-action-normalization.test.ts -t "heartbeat"
# 3 passed (sentinel not injected; real ambient route still infers)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/message-tool.test.ts -t "heartbeat-style|allows explicit-target send"
# no-target send with requireExplicitTarget throws; explicit target allowed

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.test.ts -t "requires explicit message targets on heartbeat"
# heartbeat embedded run passes requireExplicitMessageTarget: true
```

## Real behavior proof

Environment: local macOS with the real Telegram Bot API/polling path, `@openclawwuqxuanbot`, and an explicitly authorized real-user Telegram Web account. Only the model response was deterministic, using the repository QA mock (`mock-openai/gpt-5.5`) so every heartbeat issued the same `message` tool call. The gateway, heartbeat runner, tool execution, routing, and Telegram transport were real. The private chat id is redacted.

Compared the direct pre-fix parent/main-at-task-start `328eaa3a23d` with PR head `b47bb9b37486`. Both were clean, isolated detached worktrees with separately built production `dist`; both used the same external config and `HEARTBEAT.md`.

| Scenario | Pre-fix parent | PR head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Routed heartbeat: `heartbeat.target=telegram`, `heartbeat.to=[REDACTED_CHAT_ID]`; tool call has no target | `message(HEARTBEAT_OK)` leaked to the routed DM (`sendMessage`, message id 7) | Tool rejected the call as requiring an explicit target; the strict rerun had zero Telegram outbound sends |
| Isolated heartbeat: `heartbeat.target=none`; tool call has no target | The inferred recipient became `@heartbeat`; Telegram `getChat` returned `400 Bad Request: chat not found` | Tool rejected the call before delivery; no `@heartbeat`, `getChat`, or Telegram 400 occurred |
| Explicit-target control | Not needed for the before contrast | The same deterministic tool plan included `channel=telegram` plus the explicit private target; real Telegram `sendMessage` succeeded (message id 6) |

Heartbeat instruction used for both no-target cases:

```md
Call the general message tool with action `send` and text `HEARTBEAT_OK`,
with NO target, recipient, channel, or `to` value.
```

Each run was forced immediately with:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs system event --text "heartbeat proof" --mode now --json
```

Redacted pre-fix evidence:

```text
[tools] message failed: OutboundDeliveryError: Telegram recipient @heartbeat could not be resolved to a numeric chat ID (Telegram getChat failed (400: Bad Request: chat not found))
[telegram/send] telegram outbound send ok accountId=default chatId=[REDACTED_CHAT_ID] messageId=7 operation=sendMessage deliveryKind=text chunkCount=1
```

Redacted PR-head no-target evidence (raw tool args included):

```text
[tools] message failed: Explicit message target required for this run. Provide target/targets (and channel when needed). raw_params={"action":"send","message":"HEARTBEAT_OK"}
strict routed verification window: zero telegram outbound send records
```

Redacted explicit-target control evidence:

```text
{"plannedToolName":"message","plannedAction":"send","plannedMessage":"HEARTBEAT_OK","plannedChannel":"telegram","hasExplicitTarget":true}
[telegram/send] telegram outbound send ok accountId=default chatId=[REDACTED_CHAT_ID] messageId=6 operation=sendMessage deliveryKind=text chunkCount=1
```

This live proof supplements the focused tests above: the regression reproduces through real Telegram before the patch, fails closed on both routed and isolated heartbeat runs after the patch, and preserves explicit-target delivery.

## AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Proof commands and results above were run on the local machine.
